summary_paragraph: A man with a history of coronary artery disease, prior CABG, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and alcohol use disorder was admitted for left-sided chest pain and alcohol intoxication. The chest pain was atypical for acute coronary syndrome, reproducible on exam, and serial troponins were negative. A p-MIBI stress test showed normal myocardial perfusion and ejection fraction of 62%. A CTA chest ruled out pulmonary embolism or dissection but showed a left basilar opacity, likely atelectasis or early pneumonia; however, the patient lacked fever, leukocytosis, or hypoxia, so antibiotics were not continued. He was monitored for alcohol withdrawal with supportive care including thiamine and multivitamins but did not require benzodiazepines. His pain resolved during the stay, and he was discharged asymptomatic on home medications with instructions to abstain from alcohol and follow up with primary and cardiology care. Home health services were arranged.
